# Installing on Mac

Purpose: download, verify, install, update and remove the Longstead Mac app.

The Mac app is a signed and notarized download from the publisher's website and GitHub Releases. It is **not** in the Mac App Store. (The iPhone app is distributed through TestFlight first.)

## Requirements

- A Mac with **Apple silicon** (M1 or later). Intel Macs are not supported.
- **macOS 26** or later.
- Free disk space for the app plus any AI models you download (1.7 to 20.4 GB each).
- Memory: the app lists only models that fit your Mac (a model's files may take at most 45% of its memory). A Mac with 16 GB can use up to the 6.0 GB Qwen3.5 9B; 24 GB or more adds Phi-4; 48 GB or more adds the 20.4 GB Qwen3.5 35B-A3B. Smaller models and Apple's on-device model work on less.
- Optional: Apple Intelligence turned on in System Settings, if your Mac supports it, to use Apple's on-device model without downloading anything.
- An internet connection is needed only to download the app and, optionally, AI models and tax-table updates.

No Python, Homebrew, Ollama or developer tools are needed.

## 1. Download

Get the latest release from the page the publisher links for Longstead (the website or GitHub Releases). The file is a `.dmg` disk image or a `.zip` archive, for example `Retirement-Planner-macOS.dmg`. Only download from the publisher's official release page.

Each release is published with a **SHA-256 checksum**.

## 2. Verify the download (recommended)

1. Open **Terminal** (Applications > Utilities).
2. Type `shasum -a 256 ` (with a trailing space), drag the downloaded file into the Terminal window, and press Return. For example:

   ```
   shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/Retirement-Planner-macOS.dmg
   ```
3. Compare the long string of letters and numbers that appears with the SHA-256 value published for that release. They must match exactly. If they do not, delete the file and download it again from the official page.

## 3. Install

**If you downloaded a .dmg:**
1. Double-click the file.
2. Drag **Longstead** onto the **Applications** shortcut in the window.
3. Eject the disk image (right-click it in Finder's sidebar and choose Eject).

**If you downloaded a .zip:**
1. Double-click the zip to extract **Longstead**.
2. Drag the app to your **Applications** folder.

Run the app from **Applications**, not from the disk image or Downloads.

## 4. First launch and Gatekeeper

1. Open **Longstead** from Applications (double-click it, or press Command-Space and type its name).
2. Because the app was downloaded from the internet, macOS shows a notice such as "Longstead is an app downloaded from the Internet. Are you sure you want to open it?" Click **Open**. A notarized app has been checked by Apple for malicious software, and this prompt appears once.

If macOS instead says the app "can't be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software", or that it is from an unidentified developer:

- **Do not bypass it.** The copy you have may be damaged or not an official release. Delete it and download again from the official page, then repeat the checksum check.
- Check that you are on macOS 26 or later and on an Apple-silicon Mac (**Apple menu > About This Mac**). An older macOS cannot open the app and may show a message about the OS version.

To check the app's signature yourself, run this in Terminal; a good copy reports "accepted" and the source "Notarized Developer ID":

```
spctl --assess --type execute -vv "/Applications/Longstead.app"
```

## 5. First-run setup

1. The setup wizard opens in a window the first time you launch the app. Answer its questions (name, filing status, state, ages, spending, Social Security, risk). You can change everything later in **Profile**. See [QUICK_START.md](QUICK_START.md).
2. Open **Accounts** and add your accounts.
3. Choose your AI:
   - If Apple Intelligence is available, the advisors work immediately with no download.
   - Otherwise, or if you want an open-source model, open **Settings > Manage models** and download the model marked recommended. On a Mac with under 48 GB of memory that is Qwen3.5 9B (about 6.0 GB, or Qwen3.5 4B on an 8 GB Mac); with 48 GB or more it is Qwen3.5 35B-A3B (about 20.4 GB). The list shows only models that fit your Mac.
4. Review **Settings > Privacy**. See [SETTINGS_GUIDE.md](SETTINGS_GUIDE.md).

## Where your data lives

Your plans, settings, downloaded models and logs are stored in your user Library, not in the app:

`~/Library/Application Support/RetirementPlanner/`

(Finder's Library folder is hidden: choose **Go > Go to Folder...** and paste the path.) The app marks this folder as excluded from backup, so **export your plans** (Profile > Plan management > Export plan...) to keep copies. Full details are in [PRIVACY_AND_DATA.md](PRIVACY_AND_DATA.md).

## Updating

Version 1.0 does not update itself. To update:

1. Check the version you have: **Settings > About & legal** shows "Longstead <version> (<build>) by Core Hermit" at the bottom.
2. Download the newer release from the official page and verify its checksum.
3. Quit Longstead (Command-Q).
4. Drag the new app into **Applications** and choose **Replace**.
5. Open it. Your plans, settings and models are kept because they live in the folder above.

A plan exported from a newer version may not import into an older one; the app shows a message and imports nothing.

## Uninstalling

1. If you want to keep your plans, export them first (Profile > Plan management > Export plan...).
2. Quit the app.
3. Drag **Longstead** from Applications to the Trash.
4. To remove all of your data and downloaded models, also delete the folder `~/Library/Application Support/RetirementPlanner`. Deleting only the app leaves this folder (and any models, several gigabytes) behind.
5. Optional leftovers, if present: `~/Library/Preferences/com.longstead.app.plist` and `~/Library/Saved Application State/com.longstead.app.savedState`.
6. Empty the Trash.
